newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open near unchanged before cost data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open near unchanged before cost data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened near unchanged on Tuesday, facing a varied cornucopia of data, including the third-quarter employment cost index (ECI).

Analysts said, however, that while all the data being released would interest the market, price movements would be circumscribed by awareness that a full plate of economic reports still awaits the market later this week. Third-quarter GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is due on Wednesday and the October employment data and October NAPM (National Association of Purchasing Management) data will be released on Friday.
The first piece of data the market gets will be a key one -- the third-quarter Employment Cost Index (ECI).

"Everyone's expecting up 0.7 percent or up 0.8 percent for the ECI," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market analyst at CS First Boston. "If you get a number that edges up to one percent, you might knock the market back to the lows of last week's trading range," he said. On the T-bond contract, that would entail a decline to 110-12 with another stop around the 110 area, said Dimick. "The last level would probably take a second piece of bad news to reach -- like the APICS or (October Conference Board) consumer confidence data."
The APICS and consumer confidence surveys are due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, after the 0830 EST/1330 GMT release of the ECI.
But the market will also gets data at other junctures in today's trading session.
The BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales report is due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT. The Lynch Jones & Ryan Redbook weekly survey of chain-store sales is due at 1455 EST/1955 GMT.

"The data are staggered," observed Dimick. "There's potential for a small downtrade today if we are disappointed by the ECI, but nothing outside of last week's range because there are too many big releases coming."

On Wednesday, besides third-quarter GDP, which is expected to be a bond-friendly number, the market gets September home sales (a big drop is expected) and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, an anecdotal account of business and economic conditions around the nation. October employment data are due on Friday.
"You can't establish a position based on the ECI because it could get completely reversed tomorrow or the next day," said Dimick.
In early trade before the ECI release, the 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond was down 2/32 to 98-26/32, yielding 6.84 percent.
Bill rates were unchanged with three-month rates at 5.04 percent, six-month rates at 5.15 percent and year bill rates at 5.26 percent.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-28/32, yielding 5.94 percent. Five-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-26/32, yielding 6.29 percent.
The 6-1/2 percent ten-year note was down 2/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.57 percent.
